item.title: MacroMicro 🗺️ Up to 85% of revenue at CPO module makers and some server assemble
item.description:
MacroMicro
🗺️ Up to 85% of revenue at CPO module makers and some server assemblers comes from GPU customers, mostly Nvidia, which is why those stocks moved the moment news of Nvidia's leadership changes broke, even though Nvidia's own numbers kept improving. Vera Rubin generated close to US$20bn in its first quarter, full-year 2027 growth guidance went from 70% to 75%, and supply chain purchase commitments rose from US$279bn to US$390bn. Huang's return yesterday steadied all of it, yet the market has stopped paying automatically for a capacity bottleneck.

Global semiconductor sales reached US$1.24tn in January to September, up 123%, which means every node has to grow off a much higher base in 2027, and a supplier with one dominant customer has little room to absorb a single delayed order, a design revision or share lost to in-house ASICs. Export controls on remote compute and rising scrutiny of data center energy use add to that exposure.

We expect 2027 to bring divergence across the chain, with the dividing line being whether a second customer can step in the day the first one slows down. Some segments already pass that test comfortably, while others carry valuations that assume revenue arriving in 2028 or 2029.

📥 Part IV of our Outlook 2027 series divides the supply chain into two groups by how quickly a lost Nvidia order gets replaced, lists the segments in each, and shows how much of each segment's revenue comes from GPU customers. It also covers the December 1 hearing, the December 4 10-Q deadline, and the trade and licensing deadlines falling between January and June.

🔗 Full outlook: https://t.co/bXkmnss9oF

item.title: Daily Dose of Data Science You're in an ML Engineer interview at Microsoft. The
item.description:
Daily Dose of Data Science
You're in an ML Engineer interview at Microsoft.

The interviewer asks:

"Why Boosting models primarily use Trees as the base learner?

What's wrong with Linear regression or SVMs?"

You: "Because linear models can’t fit non-linear data."

Interview over.

Here's what you missed:

Texts describing boosting start with “weak learners” but then immediately pivot to trees.

But this DOES NOT mean they can only work with trees.

Consider a simple boosting algorithm:

1) Train a tree model.
2) Calculate the left-over residual.
3) Train the next model on this leftover residual.
4) Go to step 2.

Looking closely, was it really necessary to use a tree there?

All we need is the residual term, which can come from any model.

This shows that while boosting is often associated with trees, the algorithm itself is agnostic to the type of base learner used.

If you use sklearn, it is actually possible to employ a different base learner with AdaBoost.

𝗦𝗼 𝘄𝗵𝘆 𝘁𝗿𝗲𝗲𝘀?

The reason is simple.

Tabular data is quite complex:

- Variables can be skewed.
- Features can have missing values.
- Different features can have different scales.
- There can be categorical variables.
- And more.

Using standard algorithms as base learners will require extensive data cleaning and feature engineering.

But this isn’t the case with tree-based models. You can just plug them into any dataset and overfit.

Also, since we continuously add a new model to fit the left-over residuals, the distribution of the dependent variable (residual in case of regression) keeps evolving.

The feature engineering applied during the first step of boosting will likely not be helpful in the subsequent steps, requiring further manual intervention.

Using tree models, however, resolves this due to their ability to operate on any kind of data with minimal feature engineering.

👉 Over to you: What are some other reasons behind using tree models as base learners in boosting?

item.title: 我不是地主 BTC提前从黄仁勋回归的狂热情绪中冷静下来了，美股也会这样吗？接下来行情推演 上周美股大跌后，市场预期美联储不可能在股灾的情况下，加息50个基点，所
item.description:
我不是地主
BTC提前从黄仁勋回归的狂热情绪中冷静下来了，美股也会这样吗？接下来行情推演

上周美股大跌后，市场预期美联储不可能在股灾的情况下，加息50个基点，所以周六日12月的加息预期只剩下，13.6%的维持不变，和86.4%的加息25个基点

昨天晚上美股暴涨，一度还触发熔断，股灾的紧箍咒立马松了不少

市场立马从新定价美联储的预期了，今天美联储12月的加息预期从新把50个基点抬回来了

目前又剩下加息25个基点（大概率）和加息50个基点。保持不变的概率消失

目前看来股市的反弹正在给自己设置阻力，股市越涨加息50个基点的概率就会越高。美联储就会更鹰派，股市就可能会更难涨，甚至下跌

再说另一点，昨天晚上的大涨，主要是黄仁勋回归和ai情绪修复的，而非宏观大环境和通胀的彻底改善，所以不见得这一波上涨具有持续性，超跌反弹仍然是主基调

市场经过短暂的兴奋后，觉得这一波猛烈反弹不具有持续性，还是要看美联储后续发言和动作，这也是 bitcoin:native 今天大幅回撤的原因之一

所以接下来到12月9日议息会议之前，这种情况可能会加剧，就是高波动箱体震荡。至于说大幅跌破上周的低点，和继续大涨和突破昨天的高点，形成反转，这两种概率都很低

更大的行情还要等十二月之后，至于美股，高概率会收回一部分昨天晚上的涨幅，寻找一个区间选择震荡

按照上面的分析，当前市场更适合的操作就是高抛低吸，做一做区间震荡的短线单子，不要盲目赌突破和跌破前低。不然很容易导致到手的利润回吐和频繁止损

接下来还需要紧盯美元指数，和美债收益率的变动，比短期的暴涨暴跌更具有参考性

（避雷针：以上分析仅为探讨，非投资建议）
tweet

item.title: 美股金虫哥 马斯克正在推动一场可能高达3.5万亿美元的世纪大合并！ 据《金融时报》报道，Tesla和SpaceX已成立特别委员会，高盛、摩根士丹利和Everco
item.description:
美股金虫哥
马斯克正在推动一场可能高达3.5万亿美元的世纪大合并！

据《金融时报》报道，Tesla和SpaceX已成立特别委员会，高盛、摩根士丹利和Evercore等投行正式介入。

一、潜在交易条件

▪️ 交易方式：100%股票换股，非现金收购。
▪️ Tesla股价：385.46美元，市值约1.52万亿美元。
▪️ SpaceX股价：133.35美元，市值约1.81万亿美元。
▪️ 换股溢价：华尔街部分投行预计Tesla股东可能要求20%–35%的溢价。
▪️ 控制权：马斯克在合并后公司的投票权可能达到57%左右。
▪️ 最终换股比例及交易条件尚未确定。

二、对Tesla的影响
▪️ 短期利好：按照20%–35%的溢价测算，理论换股价格为463–520美元。
▪️ 长期利空：独立估值逻辑被打破，汽车业务赚的钱可能被拿去造火箭、建数据中心。
▪️ 如果合并失败，并购溢价预期也可能迅速消失。

三、对SpaceX的影响
▪️ 短期利空：如果接受上述溢价，相当于额外支付约3000亿–5300亿美元的股票对价，现有股东承担稀释压力。
▪️ 长期利弊参半：融资能力增强，但商业航天的稀缺性溢价可能被汽车业务拖累。

短期：看多Tesla的并购溢价逻辑，谨慎看待SpaceX。
长期：两家公司合并后，都可能面临10%–20%的集团估值折价风险。

更重要的是，换股不是现金收购，今天谈好的溢价，明天完全可能被股价下跌吞噬。

最大的赢家可能是马斯克——他获得了更集中的控制权、更大的融资平台，而所有梦想的成本，则由两家公司的股东共同承担。
tweet
